applicableAreas: Site-wide clearance zones around existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to determine if clearance verification exhibits are provided. Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines, transformers, pull boxes, and meters with building footprints and FFEs labeled. Sheet 9 shows electric facility locations with property lines and easement boundaries. No dedicated clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet examined. No sheet displays both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No engineered and sealed clearance exhibit sheets appear in the 39-sheet plan set.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires clearance verification exhibits to be 'engineered and scaled' and 'included in the permitted plan set' when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones. AEDC § 1.16.0(2) mandates this documentation. While the electrical design plan shows proposed structures and electric facility locations, it does not provide a dedicated exhibit demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance requirements. The absence of clearance verification exhibits means the applicant cannot demonstrate code compliance with these dual clearance envelopes, which the grouping Regulatory Overview specifies must BOTH be satisfied simultaneously—satisfying one does not satisfy the other.
findings.comment: No clearance verification exhibits provided demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance requirements from overhead distribution conductors as required by AEDC § 1.10.3. Engineered and sealed clearance exhibits must be included in the permitted plan set.

applicableAreas: All building elevations where overhangs, balconies, awnings, or canopies exist
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for profile/cross-section drawings showing clearances. Found only plan view with building footprints and FFEs; no profiles shown on this sheet. Examined Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) which contains detailed water utility profiles at 1"=20' horizontal and 1"=2' vertical scale. However, these profiles show ONLY water utility lines and do not include electric utility lines or building elements (walls, overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) needed to verify clearances from existing electric facilities. No building elevation sheets provided in the plan set that would show heights and element dimensions of proposed structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: 'Building heights are NOT shown on this plan view. There are no explicitly delineated or labeled building overhangs, balconies, or canopies that might affect vertical clearances.'
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 and the grouping 'Documents to Review' section specifically require 'Profile Drawings / Cross-section Exhibits' showing 'clearances between proposed structures and existing electric facilities/easements' with 'all building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies)' and 'dimensioned clearances.' While utility profiles exist on Sheet 20, they do not include electric utilities or building elements. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows only plan view without profiles or building element details. This deficiency prevents verification of compliance with the 7'-6" minimum clearance requirement measured from outer conductors as specified in the measurement methodology.
findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Engineered profiles drawn to scale and sealed must show vertical clearances and building element dimensions.

applicableAreas: All building elements and electric facility locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows building footprints with Finished Floor Elevations (FFEs) labeled for all 8 buildings (e.g., Bldg. 1 FFE=687.50, Bldg. 5 FFE=683.0). However, no building heights are shown. No dimensions specify clearance distances from electric facilities to building elements. Vision analysis confirmed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Transformer, pull box, and meter locations are shown but not dimensioned relative to property lines, building corners, or other reference points. No specification of clearances measured from outer conductor locations.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'Clearance dimensions and heights' to be 'specified for building elements' and 'clearances measured from outer conductor locations.' The Regulatory Overview emphasizes: 'Measure from outer conductor (the actual wire), NOT from pole centerline' and 'For three-phase overhead lines, measure from the outermost conductor farthest from the pole.' Sheet 21 contains no such dimensioning. The absence of building height dimensions, clearance measurements, and specification of measurement points from outer conductors means the plans do not demonstrate compliance with the clearance measurement methodology required by code.
findings.comment: Building element heights, clearance dimensions, and outer conductor measurement points not specified on electrical plans or profiles. All clearances must be dimensioned and measured from the outer conductor (actual wire) location, not from pole centerline.

applicableAreas: Overhead distribution electrical facilities shown on electrical and landscape plans
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 31 for clearance verification exhibits. No clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet. Sheets 9 and 21 show underground electric lines (-E- notation) and some overhead electric lines (-OHE- notation) but provide NO clearance envelope diagrams. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows one overhead electric line at bottom edge labeled '-OHE-' but includes no clearance zones, protection buffers, or clearance envelope drawings. The grouping Regulatory Overview states: 'These are separate envelopes with different geometric properties. Both must be met; satisfying one does not satisfy the other. These requirements are IN ADDITION TO NESC Section 234 baseline requirements, not substitutes for them.' No exhibits demonstrate BOTH envelope requirements simultaneously.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires dual clearance envelopes: (1) 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance, and (2) 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance. The grouping emphasizes these are separate geometric envelopes that must BOTH be satisfied. No exhibits on Sheets 9, 21, or 31 display both clearance envelopes. Sheets show overhead lines existing but provide no graphical demonstration of clearance compliance. The absence of exhibits showing both envelopes means the plans do not demonstrate code compliance with the dual clearance requirements.
findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not depict both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Both envelopes must be shown simultaneously on all required sheets.

applicableAreas: Site plan, electrical plans, utility plan
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 revealed: 'There is no explicitly labeled "Point of Service" or "Point of Delivery" on this sheet. An "Underground Electric Line" is shown entering the property from the left (Valley View Road), but it lacks a formal service designation.' Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed: 'The exact point of electric service (such as individual meters on buildings or the primary tie-in point to the grid) is NOT clearly marked with a distinct "Point of Service" or "Meter" label, nor are there specific dimensions tying a service point to building corners or property lines.' Sheet 19 shows underground electric line routing in plan view but provides no explicit service point designation. No sheet examined shows a labeled point of service with explicit dimensioning from property lines, building entry points, or other reference points. Engineer's Summary Letter mentions water and wastewater service but does NOT mention electric service point.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(5) mandates that projects with new or relocated electric service must show the proposed point of service explicitly labeled and dimensioned. The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric lines entering the property but does not designate a specific, labeled point of service. No dimensioning ties the service entry point to property boundaries or other reference features. The absence of an explicitly labeled and dimensioned point of service means the plans do not meet the basic service documentation requirement.
findings.comment: Proposed point of service not shown and labeled on all required plan sheets (electrical plans, site plan, utility plan). Point of service must be explicitly identified and dimensioned with reference to property lines and building entry points.

applicableAreas: Electrical plans and utility plan routing
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 for documentation of primary routing from service entry to buildings. Vision analysis showed: 'An "Underground Electric Line" is shown entering the property from the left (Valley View Road)' and underground lines are shown routing through the site connecting transformers to buildings. However, the path is labeled generically as 'Underground Electric Line' with no specification of routing details (distance, path, conduit size, conductor gauge, voltage). Sheet 19 shows electric line routing in plan view but similarly provides only generic '-E-' labeling without detailed routing specifications. No one-line diagram is provided showing the primary routing from the AE transformer/service point through the distribution system to individual buildings.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that plans 'Must demonstrate approximate location and appropriate space for electric facilities' and specifically address primary routing. The grouping's Service Documentation Hierarchy states 'Must identify one point of service and one service voltage (unless exceptions apply)' and plans must include 'one-line diagram of electrical riser.' While the electrical plan shows general routing of underground lines, it does not provide: (1) a one-line diagram, (2) primary routing specifications (distances, path clarity, conduit/conductor details), or (3) clear service delivery path from external source through the distribution system. The generic labeling without detailed routing information prevents verification of adequate service design.
findings.comment: Primary routing from Austin Energy service point to buildings not explicitly shown on plans, and no one-line electrical riser diagram provided. Detailed routing path and specifications must be documented, along with a one-line diagram showing service flow.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 for secondary riser configuration and one-line diagram. Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and shows transformers, pull boxes, and meters serving the buildings. However, Vision analysis confirmed: 'There is NO one-line electrical riser diagram shown on this sheet, nor is there a reference note directing the reader to one on another sheet.' The sheet shows only plan view of underground distribution with no riser configuration details for secondary service to individual buildings or units. No one-line diagram appears on any sheet reviewed (Sheets 3, 9, 19, 20, 21, 31).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electrical plans show 'one-line diagram of electrical riser' when secondary riser is part of the project design or new electric service is proposed. This 39-unit multi-family project with new electric service requires secondary service distribution to individual buildings/units. The absence of a one-line riser diagram on the electrical plans means the applicant has not provided the technical documentation required by code to show how secondary electric service is distributed from the transformers to the individual townhome units.
findings.comment: Secondary riser configuration not shown on plans and no one-line diagram of electrical riser provided. One-line riser diagram must be included on electrical plans showing secondary service distribution to all buildings and units.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 19 for electric facility labels. Found labels on all three sheets: Sheet 21 uses generic text callouts such as 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' 'Electrical Pull Box,' 'Electrical Meters,' 'Underground Electric Line.' Sheet 9 uses abbreviated notation: '-OHE-' (Overhead Electric Line), '-E-' (Underground Electric Line), and 'Transformer Pad (Typ.).' Sheet 19 uses legend notation: '-E-' for 'Proposed Underground Electric.' However, Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Facility type is identified (transformer, pull box, meter, line) but critical distinguishing information is absent.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires electric facilities to be 'clearly labeled.' While basic labels exist (e.g., 'Transformer Pad,' 'Pull Box,' 'Meter'), the grouping's Code References and Common Violations section specifies that labels should include 'facility type identification,' voltage, size, and ownership. The current labels lack this critical identifying information. Without knowing whether a transformer is customer-owned or Austin Energy-owned, or what voltage class it serves, the plans do not provide sufficient technical clarity for review and compliance verification.
findings.comment: Electric facility labels missing facility type identification (customer vs. Austin Energy owned, voltage class, capacity). All electric facilities must include clear type identification and relevant technical specifications.

applicableAreas: All electric facility labels on electrical plans
findings.observation: Examined electric facility labels on Sheets 21, 9, and 19. Sheet 21 Vision analysis showed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Labels observed: 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (no voltage, capacity, or phase information), 'Electrical Pull Box' (no conduit diameter or conductor specifications), 'Electrical Meters' (no voltage or capacity rating), 'Underground Electric Line' (no voltage, conductor gauge, or burial depth). Sheet 9 shows identical generic labeling without specifications. Sheet 19 shows only '-E-' notation without specifications. No labels include size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership information as required.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that facility labels identify not just type but include relevant technical specifications. The grouping checklist item EL-11.11 specifically requires labels to include 'size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information where applicable.' The current labels omit all of these specifications. For example: transformers lack voltage class and capacity; conduits lack diameter specifications; underground lines lack burial depth; no labels distinguish Austin Energy facilities from customer-owned facilities. This deficiency prevents reviewers and constructors from understanding the technical specifications of the electrical infrastructure.
findings.comment: Electric facility labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), and ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. All labels must include technical specifications relevant to each facility type for code compliance verification and construction clarity.

applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes sheet with legend
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 6 legend. The legend contains comprehensive utility symbols including existing and proposed electric facilities: 'Existing Power Pole & Down Guy,' 'Existing Electric Meter (E label),' 'Existing Transformer Pad (T label),' 'Existing Telephone Pedestal (T in triangle),' 'Existing Overhead Electric Line (OHE label on line),' 'Transformer Pad (T in rectangle),' 'Overhead Electric Line (OHE on line).' However, examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and found NO legend block on this sheet. Vision analysis confirmed: 'There is NO legend present on this specific sheet to define the symbols used.' The electrical design plan uses symbols such as '-OHE-' and '-E-' but does not define them locally. The plan relies on cross-reference to Sheet 3 legend, but no note on Sheet 21 directs readers to Sheet 3 for symbol definitions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Electric facility symbols' be 'identified in legend.' While a legend exists on Sheet 3, it is NOT on the electrical design plan itself (Sheet 21). Users of Sheet 21 must consult an external sheet (Sheet 3) to understand the symbols. This violates the principle that each plan sheet should be self-contained or have clear cross-references. The absence of legend identification on the electrical plan sheet means symbols used on Sheet 21 are not identified on that specific sheet as required by code.
findings.comment: Electric facility symbols not identified in legend on electrical plan sheet. Legend defining all electric facility symbols must be present on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) or have an explicit cross-reference note directing users to the legend location.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) for electric facility display. Vision analysis revealed: 'Electric facilities are generally NOT prominently featured on this landscape plan. I do not see transformers, meters, or pull boxes depicted or labeled. There is one utility line shown: An overhead electric line indicated by a line with the text "-OHE-" running horizontally along the bottom edge of the site plan.' The overhead electric line shown is at minimal scale with only the '-OHE-' label; no transformer symbols, pad locations, meter locations, or underground line routing is depicted on the landscape plan. The vision analysis noted: 'Because there are no clearance zones marked, this visual overlap suggests a potential conflict between the overhead lines and the tree canopies,' indicating the electric line is difficult to distinguish from landscape features at the sheet scale.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1) requires that plans show 'electric facilities' at 'legible scale' on 'required plans,' and the grouping's Documents to Review specifies that electric facilities must be shown on 'Landscape Plan' with facilities 'clearly visible.' While the landscape plan (Sheet 31) contains one minimally-labeled overhead electric line, electric facilities are not shown 'clearly and at legible scale' as required. Transformers, pull boxes, underground lines, and easements are absent. The single overhead line shown without clearance zones or protection buffers makes it difficult to distinguish from landscape elements and does not provide the visual clarity required for landscape coordination.
findings.comment: Electric facilities not shown clearly and at legible scale on landscape plan, or symbols too small to distinguish. Transformer locations, pull boxes, underground electric line routing, and electric easements must be shown on the landscape plan at adequate scale for visual coordination with landscaping.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) titled 'Utility Tap Plan showing proposed water and wastewater connections.' Vision analysis showed: 'The entire drawing provided on this page is a top-down, "plan view" layout of the site' at 'Scale 1" = 20'.' The sheet shows water, wastewater, and storm drain utilities prominently with detailed labeling and DFU calculations. However, electric utility documentation is minimal—only a generic '-E-' (Proposed Underground Electric) line shown in legend and plan view routing, with no detail, specification, or emphasis. The electric routing shares plan space with water/wastewater systems without adequate separation or clarity. No profile view of electric utilities is shown (note: profiles shown are water-only). The utility plan does not 'fill the page' with adequate scale for electric facility detail—Sheet 19 appears to focus on water/wastewater with electric facilities shown secondarily.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Utility plan' be 'provided at adequate scale to fill page, resulting in excessive white space and insufficient detail.' The grouping's checklist item EL-11.20 specifies that the utility plan should not have 'excessive white space and insufficient detail.' While Sheet 19 at 1"=20' scale is technically correct, the electric utilities are shown with minimal detail and labeling compared to water/wastewater systems. The lack of electrical profile information and detailed routing specifications suggests the electric utility documentation may not fill adequate page space or provide sufficient detail. An electrically-focused utility plan sheet or enhanced electric documentation on Sheet 19 would be more adequate.
findings.comment: Utility plan scale or layout may not be adequate for clear display of electric utilities. If electric utilities are shown on the utility plan, they must be at sufficient scale with adequate labeling and detail to distinguish from other utilities and allow clear review.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 21, and 19 for electric utility easement delineation. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed: 'There are specific callouts for easements on the right (East) and bottom right (Southeast) of the plan: On the far right side... "5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx." In the bottom right corner, text reads: "5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx." At the top right corner, there is a "5' P.U.E. Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx."' These easements are labeled with record references and widths. Easements shown on Sheets 9, 21, and 19 with dashed lines and labels. However, facts.md reveals critical oversight: 'Two easements NOT depicted on submitted site plan': Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 ac, NE interior) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 ac, NE corner). These two critical easements are not shown on the site plan.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires all 'Electric utility easements' be 'clearly delineated.' While some easements are shown, the facts.md document identifies two major recorded easements (Greenbelt, Drainage) that are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan. Their absence prevents verification that the proposed buildings and utilities do not conflict with these recorded restrictions.
findings.comment: Electric utility easements not clearly delineated on plans. Two recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, City of Austin Drainage Easement) are missing from the site plan. All recorded electric and related utility easements must be clearly shown with locations, extents, and width dimensions.

applicableAreas: Electric facility plans (Site Plan, Utility Plan)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) for property lines. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Yes, property lines are clearly shown using a heavy dashed/dotted line type, accompanied by bearing and distance callouts (e.g., "N63° 32' 57"W 414.24'" along the bottom boundary).' Property lines ARE shown on Sheet 9. Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for property lines. Vision analysis noted property boundaries are shown on the electrical design plan with easement references. However, examined facts.md and found critical discrepancy regarding property delineation: Site area stated as 2.16 acres on site plan; 2019 deed states 2.158 ac; TCAD states 2.1970 ac; COA GIS parcel measures 2.111 ac. Additionally, legal description and boundaries may not fully account for two missing recorded easements (Greenbelt 0.31 ac, Drainage 0.130 ac). Building setbacks are shown via dimensions on Site Plan (e.g., 26.1' from western boundary to Bldg. 1, 21.3' from southern boundary to Bldg. 8) but are NOT labeled as explicit 'Building Setback' lines.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(v) requires 'Property lines and building setbacks' be shown on 'electric facility plans (site plan, utility plan).' While property lines are clearly shown with bearings and distances on Sheet 9, building setbacks are not explicitly labeled with 'Building Setback' or 'B.L.' designations. The setback distances exist as dimension calls but are not formally delineated as setback lines. Additionally, the property lines themselves may not accurately represent the controlled property given the missing easement areas documented in facts.md. Building setback lines should be explicitly drawn and labeled, not implied through scattered dimensional callouts.
findings.comment: Building setbacks not clearly shown on electric facility plans. While property lines are delineated, explicit building setback lines and labels must be shown on the site plan and utility plan to clearly establish the required buffer zones for electric facility planning.

applicableAreas: All electric facility locations and easements
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21 for documentation demonstrating Austin Energy personnel access to electric facilities. Sheet 21 shows transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground line routing throughout the site. Easement areas are shown (5' Electric Easements on eastern and southern boundaries per vision analysis). However, no plans explicitly demonstrate or document that 'development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities.' No access pathways are labeled, no clearance zones for equipment trucks are designated, no maintenance access widths are specified. No notes on the plans state that a 20-foot equipment access corridor is maintained, or that easement roads support required vehicle loads. The grouping's Regulatory Overview mentions transmission easement road requirements (46,000 lb tandem axle) but no plans show access provisions for electric distribution facilities.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(4) requires that 'Plans must demonstrate that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities.' The electrical design plan shows facility locations but does not explicitly document how access for maintenance, repair, or emergency response will be maintained. No access roads, clearance zones, or turning radiuses are shown or dimensioned. No notes certify that Austin Energy has adequate access to transformers, vaults, or other equipment for routine or emergency operations. The absence of access documentation means the plans do not affirmatively demonstrate code compliance with the access requirement.
findings.comment: Plans do not explicitly demonstrate that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities. Access pathways, maintenance clearance zones, and vehicle turning radiuses must be shown and documented to ensure Austin Energy can access and maintain all electric infrastructure.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for projected load information. The sheet contains: building unit counts (e.g., Bldg. 1: 3 units, Bldg. 2: 6 units), square footage per building, and FFE data. No projected electrical load (in kW, amperage, or kVA) is labeled on the sheet. No demand calculation is shown. No specification of service amperage or phases is documented. No load table is provided. The grouping's Service Documentation Hierarchy specifies 'New service >350A single-phase or >225A three-phase: AE Design review required' but no amperage or load documentation is shown to indicate whether this threshold applies or what the design service parameters are.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires 'Projected load' to be 'provided on electrical plans' for projects with 'new or upgraded electric service.' This 39-unit multi-family project requires new electric service, triggering the requirement. The electrical design plan shows physical layout of distribution infrastructure but does not quantify the electrical load that infrastructure must serve. Without projected load documentation, reviewers cannot verify that the service size, transformer capacity, and distribution infrastructure are adequate for the intended use. The grouping's threshold of 350A/225A for AE Design Review cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load not provided on electrical plans. Estimated demand load in amperes (or kVA) must be calculated and shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan to demonstrate adequate service sizing.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and found CAD file path printed on sheet: 'P:\01_PROJECTS\AUSTIN\2023\2023-010-00 VALLEY VIEW TOWNHOMES\04_CAD\02_SHEETS\UTILITY ELEC PLAN.dwg 2/28/2024 10:11 AM Chris_Rodgers.' The CAD file path is present and indicates file version and timestamp. However, no explicit statement appears on the sheet indicating that CAD files were georeferenced with 'NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system' as required by UCM § 1.4.2.6. The grouping's Regulatory Overview specifies: 'Georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system.' This is a technical specification of the CAD file that cannot be verified from the printed plan sheet alone—it requires examining the actual DXF/DWG file properties.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires CAD files to be 'Georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system.' This is a technical file property that cannot be verified from the printed sheet—it requires examining the DXF/DWG file metadata directly. The sheet shows a CAD file exists but does not indicate its coordinate system. Without access to the actual CAD file properties, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: CAD file georeferencing cannot be verified from plan sheets. CAD files must be verified to be georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system with all electric facilities in model space and UCS set to 'World'.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for indication that electric facilities are on correct CAD layers and colored in Magenta per UCM § 1.4.2.6 layer standards. Vision analysis noted: 'The electrical routing and symbols are rendered in blue' on the printed sheet. The printed sheet shows blue coloring for underground and overhead electric lines. However, printed plan sheets typically display colors differently than the original CAD file colors. The grouping's Regulatory Overview specifies that electric facilities must be on 'separate layers with magenta color: Electric UG Lines: Layer "Elec. UG", Electric OH Lines: Layer "Elec. OH", Electric Poles: Layer "Elec. Pole", etc.' The blue color shown on the printed sheet does not match the required Magenta color specification, but this could be a printing/display artifact rather than evidence of incorrect CAD coloring.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires electric facilities be 'on separate layers with magenta color' using specified layer names (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. MH, etc.). The printed plan shows blue coloring, which does not match the Magenta specification. However, printed colors often differ from CAD file colors due to print settings, paper medium, and color calibration. To definitively verify layer and color compliance, the actual DXF/DWG file must be examined for layer structure and color properties. From the printed sheet alone, only blue-colored display is observable, which contradicts the Magenta requirement but may not conclusively prove CAD file non-compliance without examining the source file.
findings.comment: Cannot definitively verify correct CAD layer assignment and Magenta color specification from printed sheets. CAD files must be verified to contain electric facilities on correct layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. MH, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Pole) with Magenta color as specified in UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 CAD file path shown on printed sheet: 'P:\01_PROJECTS\AUSTIN\2023\2023-010-00 VALLEY VIEW TOWNHOMES\04_CAD\02_SHEETS\UTILITY ELEC PLAN.dwg' This indicates a DWG file exists. The grouping's Regulatory Overview specifies that required objects must be 'in model space with UCS setting to "World"' per UCM § 1.4.2.6. This is a technical CAD file property that cannot be verified from the printed sheet—it requires opening the DWG file and checking the model space / UCS properties. The printed sheet does not contain any notation indicating model space/UCS settings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires CAD files to have 'All required objects in model space with UCS setting to "World".' This is a technical file property that cannot be verified by examining the printed plan sheet. Verification requires opening the DWG/DXF file and checking object placement and UCS configuration. Without access to the actual CAD file, this requirement cannot be verified from the plan sheets alone.
findings.comment: Cannot verify model space and UCS settings from printed sheets. CAD files must be verified to have all required objects in model space with UCS setting to 'World' per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for building heights. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Building heights are NOT shown on this plan view.' Buildings 1-8 show square footage and FFE (Finished Floor Elevation) but no height dimension. Examined Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) looking for building height information. The guide.md for Sheet 11 lists Building FFEs (e.g., Bldg. 1 FFE=687.50) but does not mention building heights or roof elevations. No building elevation sheets showing heights (facades with dimensions) appear to be included in the 39-sheet plan set. The README lists sheets 1-39; no dedicated building elevation sheet is identified. The grouping's Documents to Review lists 'Building Elevations - Building heights and element dimensions (overhangs, balconies, awnings) for clearance verification' as a required document. No such sheet was located.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(iii) requires 'Permanent structures' be shown 'with both footprint and height on plans.' While building footprints are shown on the electrical design plan and other sheets, building heights are NOT shown. Finished Floor Elevations provide vertical data but do NOT indicate roof heights or total building heights. No building elevation sheets showing heights and overhangs are provided. The absence of height documentation on permanent structures is a deficiency that prevents verification of clearances to electric facilities and other code compliance matters.
findings.comment: Permanent structures not shown with both footprint and height on plans. Building elevation sheets must be provided showing building heights, roof lines, and all element dimensions (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) for clearance verification.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) which shows 'existing and proposed topography, establish building finished floor elevations (FFEs), map storm drainage infrastructure, and indicate the location of retaining walls and utility easements.' Sheet 11 shows contour lines, building FFEs, and drainage infrastructure. Examined Sheet 15 which addresses 'Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations' and references detention pond design. Sheet 21 (Electrical) shows final site layout with utilities. However, the grouping's requirement specifies 'final proposed topology including grades, grade changes, floodplains, and detention ponds for electric facility review.' While grading and detention ponds ARE shown, explicit coordination documenting how the final topology interacts with the electric facilities (especially underground lines and easements) is not provided. No plan explicitly states 'electric facilities are/are not located in floodplain areas' or confirms underground electric line routing accommodates proposed grading/slopes, or that detention pond construction will not impact easement access.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires plans 'show final proposed topology including grades, grade changes, floodplains, and detention ponds for electric facility review.' While the site plan shows grades, changes, and detention pond, explicit documentation coordinating these elements WITH the electric facilities (line depths relative to grades, easement access through detention areas, floodplain impacts) is not provided. The requirement specifically states this topography information must be shown 'for electric facility review'—meaning it must be reviewed in the context of electric infrastructure, not separately.
findings.comment: Plans do not explicitly demonstrate that proposed topology (grades, grade changes, floodplains, detention ponds) will not adversely impact electric facilities. Grading plan must coordinate with electrical infrastructure to confirm adequate clearances and access are maintained for all electric facilities.
